subject: Standby activation eligibility & SLA exception request — FinTrust (EU)

From: Alina Petros <alina.petros@fintrustbank.com>

Cc: procurement@fintrustbank.com, CloudRisk Team <cloudrisk@fintrustbank.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 08:17:00 +0100
Subject: Standby activation eligibility & RTO/RPO ask

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're excited about Redwood's performance; the latency profile looked good for our bursty reconciliation workloads. As we've been working with CloudRisk and Procurement, a few compliance constraints in our EU region mean we can't accept the standard 60-minute warm-standby RTO for a subset of our regulated portfolios.

Specifically, the RegOps team requires:
- A documented confirmation of data residency during failover (EU-only)
- An RTO of 4 hours for the Regulated Partition (instead of 60 mins) with an RPO of 2 hours
- A limited SLA carveout window (only applies to warm-standby activation events caused by cross-region network partitions)

Our procurement team asked whether Redwood would approve a formal SLA exception and provide a one-off pricing credit to reflect the narrower activation guarantees. I've attached our requirements workbook for reference.

Can you confirm next steps and whether Redwood can sign an exception addendum?

Best,
Alina
FinTrust Bank — Senior Manager, Cloud SRE

Subject: Re: Standby activation eligibility & RTO/RPO ask

Hi all — I reviewed the workbook and sketched a short risk/mitigation summary. Attaching the DR architecture diagram and a draft of our exception template.

Key technical notes:
- We can guarantee EU-only data residency for the Regulated Partition by scoping VPC peering and storage to EU regions and preventing automatic cross-region cache replication for those datasets.
- The default warm-standby activation flow (60-minute target) relies on auto-scaling + KV cache warmup. For the regulated service the warm cache cannot be allowed to replicate out-of-region, so achieving 60 minutes is materially harder; 4 hours RTO is a reasonable negotiated target.
- RPO at 2 hours is feasible if the customer is willing to accept asynchronous snapshotting to an EU-only S3 bucket with durable retention.

Operational compensations we recommend:
1) Quarterly DR drills that Redwood runs jointly with FinTrust (documented runbooks).
2) A rollback SLA that reduces liability on auto-failovers tied to manual approval windows.
3) A one-time service credit (we can propose levels) if an activation exceeds agreed thresholds.

See attachments: DR_Architecture_Diagram.png, Redwood_SLA_Exception_Template.docx

Happy to discuss on the call.

— Aditya
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
Attachment: DR_Architecture_Diagram.png; Redwood_SLA_Exception_Template.docx

Attached is a short commercial proposal: we recommend a one-time implementation & assurance credit equal to 6% of the first-year committed spend for the regulated partition, plus an ongoing 5% discount on standby capacity for 12 months. This is conditional on FinTrust agreeing to the quarterly DR drills and the activation trigger annex that Aditya will finalize.

We can produce a DocuSign addendum using the attached exception template. If that works, Mina and I will run the final review and route to Legal. I'll put a redline-ready DocuSign link once you sign off.

Next steps / asks for FinTrust:
- Confirm acceptance of the proposed credit structure (one-time 6% + 12-month 5% standby discount)
- Confirm two names from CloudRisk that will sign the technical annex
- Book the 30-minute technical call (Aditya suggested two slots below)
